# MCP Skills Extension (SEP-2640)

**What this answers:** What the Skills Over MCP working group is proposing,
how it works technically, and whether it matters for someone already writing
skills as local files.

**Key insight:** Two separate things are happening. The **format** (Agent
Skills / SKILL.md) is already a mature standard adopted by 26+ platforms [15].
The **transport** (SEP-2640 / skill:// over MCP Resources) is a draft
proposal — In Review, no client ships native support yet [13][14]. If you
write SKILL.md files today, your format is already compatible. Nothing
needs to change until clients adopt skill://.

## Quick Status

| Component | Status | Your Action |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| Agent Skills format (SKILL.md) | Mature — 26+ platforms (single-source claim [15]), 40K+ skills [15] | Already using it |
| SEP-2640 transport (skill://) | Draft — In Review since April 2026 [13] | Watch, don't act |
| MCP client support | None — no native skill:// support [14] | Nothing to adopt yet |
| Model adherence to skills | Unreliable — adherence degrades as context grows ("time-decaying") [7] | Transport doesn't fix this |

## What SEP-2640 Proposes

Skills served as MCP Resources via `skill://` URIs [3]:
- `skill://git-workflow/SKILL.md` — read via standard `resources/read`
- Optional `skill://index.json` for discovery
- No new protocol methods — reuses existing Resources primitive
- Security: skills are untrusted input, no implicit execution

**Value over local files:** dynamic updates, cross-server composition,
ephemeral availability, enterprise RBAC/audit [4][6].

**When local files suffice:** standalone skills, single-user, no server
coupling, existing infrastructure works [4].

## Portability Caveat

Claude Code-specific frontmatter fields (`hooks`, `agent`, `model`,
`context`) are outside the Agent Skills spec's 6 allowed fields [11][12].
Skills using these work locally but are not portable to other platforms
and cannot be meaningfully served over MCP (hooks require host execution,
which MCP skills prohibit without user approval) [3].
